subject: Initial-token SLA checklist & benchmark plan for ClearCare MAP
messages:
From: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@clearcare.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-02T12:15:00-04:00
Subject: Kickoff: ClearCare MAP — perf gating and initial latency targets

Hi Marcus / Laura,

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier today. Attached is our draft MAP and a short list of high-priority acceptance criteria we care about for chat streaming: primarily initial-token latency (TTFT), streaming steady-state latency, and concurrency.

High-level ask: can Redwood run a focused benchmark against our sample prompt set and confirm whether the hosted Dedicated profile (ds-small-d) meets the following acceptance targets? If not, we need a clear remediation plan in the MAP.

Attachments: MAP-draft-clearcare-v1.pdf (draft MAP, milestones)

Can you confirm availability to run the bench the week of Aug 3? We’re hoping to finalize the MAP and sign by Aug 20 if gates are green.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short sync if helpful.

Sara
Sara Bennett
Head of Product, ClearCare AI
sara.bennett@clearcare.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@clearcare.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-02T15:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: ClearCare MAP — perf gating and initial latency targets

Hi Sara,

Appreciate the MAP draft — reviewed and added a short perf plan (attached). We can run a Redwood-hosted benchmark against the sample prompts. Proposed next steps:

- We run a controlled bench from our us-west-2 dedicated pool on Aug 4 10:00 PT (2h slot) using the provided prompt set.
- Deliverables: raw token-level logs, aggregated p50/p95/p99 for initial token (TTFT), subsequent-token latencies, and sustained concurrency throughput.
- We’ll include two model variants: rdx-3b-int8 (primary) and rdx-7b-qat (fallback) to show graceful degradation.

Attached: redwood-perf-plan-v1.xlsx (bench harness settings and measurement points).

Laura / Stephanie — tagging you for technical acceptance criteria and any specific test harness notes.

Marcus
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@clearcare.ai>
Date: 2026-08-03T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: ClearCare MAP — perf gating and initial latency targets

Thanks — adding technical acceptance criteria and runbook notes. Please see inline acceptance gating we want in the MAP.

Acceptance gating (recommended):
- Initial-token TTFT (first byte/token produced when streaming): p50 <= 120 ms, p95 <= 350 ms, p99 <= 700 ms.
- Subsequent-token latency (steady-state per-token emit): p50 <= 15 ms, p95 <= 45 ms, p99 <= 120 ms.
- Streaming tail latency (time between client ack and token visible for downstream): p50/p95/p99 — measured as 10/50/200 ms targets respectively (example metric name: streaming_emit_latency_ms).
- Concurrency: sustain 50 concurrent active chat sessions with the 512-token context typical for ClearCare prompts (tokenization note in spreadsheet).
- Throughput: no >5% error rate, no model OOMs; KV cache hit behavior documented.

Test harness specifics (what Redwood will run):
- Warmup: 30-minute warmup with representative prefixes to populate KV cache and enable batching curves.
- Batching policy: dynamic batching up to 32 requests/step; measure both continuous batching and single-request latency.
- Environment: us-west-2 Dedicated pool, GPU profile: A10G-equivalent.
- Measurement: token-level timestamps, request ingress timestamp, model emit timestamp, response completion.

Please provide: sample prompts (JSONL), expected top-level instructions, any safety filters that might affect streaming behavior. Also confirm if you need quantized model comparisons in the deliverable.

Marcus / Stephanie / Laura,

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@clearcare.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-05T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: ClearCare MAP — perf gating and initial latency targets (bench results + next steps)

Sara / team,

Thanks again for the prompt set and warmup file. We executed the Redwood-hosted benchmark on Aug 4 (us-west-2 Dedicated node pool) with the configuration in redwood-perf-plan-v1.xlsx. Below is a concise summary and next steps for the MAP. Full raw logs and CSV attached (bench-results-2026-08-04.csv).

Summary of key latency/throughput numbers (rdx-3b-int8 primary, rdx-7b-qat fallback):
- Initial-token TTFT (primary): p50 = 95 ms, p95 = 310 ms, p99 = 620 ms.
- Subsequent-token latency (primary): p50 = 12 ms, p95 = 38 ms, p99 = 115 ms.
- Streaming emit latency (measured end-to-end): p50 = 9 ms, p95 = 48 ms, p99 = 210 ms.
- Sustained concurrency: we sustained 60 concurrent active chat sessions (512-token context) for 30 minutes with <1% error rate.
- Fallback behavior: rdx-7b-qat showed ~20% higher TTFT at p95 but preserved throughput under peak load.

Observations & recommended MAP remediation clauses:
- KV cache warmup materially reduces p95 TTFT for stateful prompts — include a 15–30 minute warmup milestone in the MAP before go-live.
- For worst-case p99 reduction, we recommend enabling dynamic batching caps and a soft concurrency limit at the application layer (recommended default: 75 concurrent users per pool).
- If ClearCare requires p95 < 250 ms for initial-token in all cases, we should scope a dedicated GPU profile (higher-memory instance) or additional burst capacity in the MAP (cost implications captured in the attached XLSX).

Deliverables attached:
- bench-results-2026-08-04.csv (token-level timestamps + aggregated metrics)
- updated MAP comment set (we’ll push edits to the shared Drive folder).

Next steps (action owners):
- Redwood (Marcus / Stephanie): push updated MAP with the warmup and burst-cap clauses by Aug 6.
- ClearCare (Sara / Jordan): confirm if p95 initial-token acceptance can be relaxed to 350 ms or if you need the hard 250 ms target.
- Procurement sync: Laura to coordinate order-form countersignature timeline.

If helpful we can run a targeted p99 reduction pass (profiling kernel hotspots) next week — that would be an engineering deep-dive, ETA 5 business days.

Marcus
Director, Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
Attachments: bench-results-2026-08-04.csv
